ar_crescent_war_bonnet_area.blurb: A compact pocket of 19 boulder problems tucked into the Idaho Boulders on the west side of Horseshoe Canyon Ranch, north-central Arkansas. The sandstone problems start around V1, with the bulk landing between V3 and V9 and a single V14 at the top end. Two moderates anchor the zone, the V3 Crescent and the V5 Warbonnet, which makes it a worthwhile stop for climbers working through the middle grades. Landings are described as good and the stone as excellent. It is a short uphill hike from the main parking area, passing other boulder clusters on the way, and a narrow corridor leads to a small room holding several of the problems.

ar_chickenhead_wall.blurb: Chickenhead Wall is the first wall on East Main Bluff at Sam's Throne in north-central Arkansas, with 19 sandstone routes split between trad and sport. Most of the climbing sits between 5.6 and 5.10, with a handful of harder lines near 5.11 and 5.12, so it suits climbers stepping up from the moderate grades. The wall is a low-angle slab covered in large holds, set behind a big freestanding boulder, and its routes continue past a large cave toward the neighboring Reality Wall. Roof cracks near the corridor behind the boulder give short, sturdy trad pitches. Many parties arrive by walking in from the top of the bluff.

ar_adventure_supply_alley.blurb: Adventure Supply Alley is one of three sections of City Rock Bluff, a long sandstone band above the White River in northeast Arkansas near Calico Rock. It holds a varied mix: easy sport lines, a few demanding top-rope problems, moderate trad climbs and some boulder problems. Roped routes run from about 5.5 into the 5.12 range, and the boulders span V2 to V10, so there is something for beginners and for stronger climbers alike. The setting is quiet compared with the state's busier crags. Reaching it takes a short trail walk from the overlook, then a scramble down through a gap between boulders to the base.

ar_arcade_the.blurb: The Arcade is a northeast-facing sandstone wall on the west side of Horseshoe Canyon Ranch in north-central Arkansas, sitting beside the Ren and Stimpy and Street Fighter walls. It has 19 routes, mostly bolted sport lines with a few trad climbs, running from the 5.8 range through 5.11. Moderates dominate, with 5.8 and 5.9 lines making up over half, and a good number of 5.10s to follow. The wall stays shaded for most of the day, which helps in warm weather, and this side of the ranch is rarely crowded. Climbs here run a little taller than those at some other ranch sectors.

ar_flux_pavilion.blurb: Flux Pavilion is a single sandstone boulder in Mossy Bluff, a city park at Heber Springs in northeast Arkansas, and it holds the largest cluster of problems in the park. The 19 problems run from V0 to V12, though most fall between V0 and V4 with a scattering of harder lines above. Climbing is powerful and varied, and it works well as a local circuit for training and linking problems. The stone is soft and friable, and footholds low down tend to be sandy, so brush before you pull on. It is a short walk of about a minute from where you park, and it is not a destination crag.
